title: Ex-offenders Assisted under Jobs Growth Incentive Scheme
what_it_is: Ex-offenders Assisted under Jobs Growth Incentive Scheme

sections.label: JGI support for ex-offenders
sections.summary: JGI supported hiring of about 2,300 ex-offenders as at May 2022, with top 10 sectors accounting for over eight in 10 hires.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Based on the latest available data, the Jobs Growth Incentive (JGI) has supported the hiring of approximately 2,300 ex-offenders as at May 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The top 10 sectors which have employed ex-offenders with JGI support are as follows: environmental services, logistics, food services, wholesale trade, construction, retail, professional services, food manufacturing, precision engineering and real estate.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: These sectors collectively account for over eight in 10 ex-offenders hired with JGI support.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Employers who hire ex-offenders directly through YRSG, Industrial and Services Co-operative Society or halfway houses engaged by the Singapore Prison Service will automatically receive JGI if they meet the eligibility criteria for JGI.

sections.label: JGI sunset after March
sections.summary: JGI is not permanent and other YRSG employment support measures will continue for ex-offenders and employers beyond March 2023.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: With regards to post-March when the JGI programme is sunset, I want to also reiterate that the JGI is an extraordinary measure and this was introduced during COVID-19 to support employers to expand local hiring and is not a permanent – not envisaged and not planned to be a permanent scheme.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: As we speak, there are other employment support measures today by YRSG and these will continue to be available to ex-offenders and employers beyond March 2023.

sections.label: Yellow Ribbon support question
sections.summary: Minister says JGI's success with ex-offenders is not linearly correlated to Yellow Ribbon support, citing COVID-19 and JGI's economy-wide support of three quarters of a million people.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I just wonder if the Minister, in light of the fact that as he explained, the JGI was so extraordinarily successful with helping with the placement of ex-offenders, whether this suggest to him that the Yellow Ribbon scheme, in and of itself, might actually be under-providing the kind of support that would be necessary to help with the rehabilitation of ex-offenders?

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: I do not think it is a linear correlated type of relationship, because the real big issue over the last two and a half years has been COVID-19 and the externality, the black swan event, was so huge that, if you look at the JGI across the board for the entire economy and industry, it has supported three quarters of a million people.

sections.label: Targeted JGI and confidentiality
sections.summary: Minister says policies are reviewed to help ex-offenders get and stay in employment, and a targeted JGI for ex-offenders raises how to protect their confidentiality status.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: My point is that, moving forward, as I have said, we continue to review, to tweak the policies to see how we can help our ex-offenders to get gainful employment, even faster and stay in gainful employment even faster.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: But if we sunset the entire JGI scheme and we maintain it for a very targeted group of people, particularly the ex-offenders, then obviously it brings to mind, how do we protect the confidentiality status of this group of people.
